prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots put GLP-1 first, but unanimity is not the argument. The scientific case is that the chain runs from proglucagon processing, through identification of the insulinotropic GLP-1(7-36) amide and its human physiology, to receptor-based pharmacology that has been confirmed in large randomized outcome trials across glycaemia, body weight, cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The mechanism is stable and independently replicated, and the clinical consequence is very large and still growing. A prize built on Holst (physiology and secretion in humans), Drucker (receptor biology, proglucagon-derived peptides, translational mechanism) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active peptide) rewards the discovery itself, which is what the prize is for, and keeps the citation scientifically precise.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is credit. Three seats cannot hold four credited names, and any trio is a contestable allocation. Mojsov's priority relative to the Habener group, which is not among the credited names, is publicly disputed, and I cannot verify the details from the supplied material. Leaving out Lotte Bjerre Knudsen means the prize would honour the physiology but not the pharmacology that turned it into durable long-acting drugs. A discovery-only prize that leaves out the drug-development step could be seen as incomplete, and one that includes it could be seen as shifting toward industrial development.

responses.point: Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is the preferred trio. Mojsov is left out because the weight of her contribution is disputed, and Knudsen is included as the pharmacological step that produced long-acting agonists.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen point seriously. Semaglutide and liraglutide are what made the physiology matter at scale, and I do not regard her contribution as lesser. But a disputed attribution is not the same as a weak one. Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) form is a discovery-level step that the later drugs depend on, and I would not drop her only because the priority record is untidy. Where I agree with you is that the committee has to decide openly between a physiology-only and a physiology-plus-drug-development framing. If colleagues think that framing should decide the third seat, I would reopen it rather than treat my trio as settled.

responses.point: Drucker, Holst and Mojsov are the strongest scientific trio. Knudsen's work is drug development that sits more naturally in industry, and Mojsov's priority is contested and needs careful adjudication.
responses.response: I agree with the trio but I am less comfortable with the argument that industrial drug development belongs outside the prize. Many prizes in this field have honoured people who made a mechanism usable as a therapy, so the setting alone should not exclude Knudsen. The better reason to exclude her is the three-seat limit and the fact that the discovery chain is complete without her. I agree that the Mojsov priority question needs adjudication. I would want that done on the primary publication record before the final ballot, not on recollection, and I would flag now that I cannot do it from the profile material alone.

responses.point: Drucker, Holst and Mojsov form a coherent trio, and Knudsen is left out to stay within three. He ranks BCL-2 and TOR near the top after the GLP-1 and CAR-T/UPR candidates, and treats B010 as a compact, long-overdue pair.
responses.response: We agree on the first-place configuration, and I am noting that so it is not mistaken for independent confirmation of a view we both reached in the same way. Where we differ is on B010. You rank it third and I rank it third as well, but I would press the point you made about therapeutic payoff. The UPR case rests mainly on fundamental physiology, and ISRIB-type modulators are still prospective. I think B010 is a strong alternative and a credible second part, but I would not let it displace a disease-linked discovery unless the committee agrees that a basic-mechanism prize is wanted this year.

responses.point: GLP-1 is first, with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen. B008 is second, and B023 (imatinib) is placed above B010. He notes that optogenetics is a method award, which the committee weighs against disease-relevant discoveries.
responses.response: The method-versus-disease point is the right one to raise against B005. I ranked it second on originality and reach, but the attribution problem is severe, with six credited names, three seats, and a real dispute over neuronal demonstration. For that reason I now treat it as an alternative rather than a leading second part. I disagree with ranking B023 above B010. The imatinib story is clinically exceptional, but the credited trio leaves out the upstream BCR-ABL oncogene work, which is a larger completeness problem than the Ron and Kaufman question in the UPR.

responses.point: GLP-1 goes first with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. B005, B010 and B049 follow, with B005 second on methodological impact, and Sandberg treats the allocation between basic hormone biology and drug development as unresolved.
responses.response: We share the same trio, and I agree the basic-versus-development allocation is open. I would qualify your placement of B005 second. The impact on physiology is real, but a prize shared with B043 would need three or fewer names in total, and a two-part configuration involving B005 would force an unacceptable cut among the optogenetics contributors. I regard B010 as the cleaner companion to the incretin prize, since Walter and Mori are a compact pair with settled credit.

uncertainties: Whether the third seat in B043 should go to Mojsov (identification of the active peptide) or Knudsen (long-acting agonists), and how the Habener group's claim bears on Mojsov's priority. This needs the primary record.
Whether the committee wants a physiology-only citation or one that also recognises drug development.
Whether a second part is possible at all. A one-part B043 trio leaves no room, so a two-part prize would force a smaller incretin group.
Whether B010 rests mainly on fundamental physiology and whether the omission of Ron and Kaufman weakens it.
My knowledge of priority details for several candidates comes from recollection and is not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent with B043 or the alternatives B010 and B005 from my profile. I record that my profile lists about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (count not audited), on dopamine neurons, Nurr1 and autophagy, and that I was a postdoctoral fellow with Paul Greengard. Neither involves a credited name on B043, B010 or B005. My opening ballot placed B014 (Benabid, deep brain stimulation) eighth, and I noted that my clinical familiarity with Parkinson's disease should not inflate it. It is not in my preferred configuration.
